title: Tigers can swim across 8 km of water

scenes.headline: This big cat is a strong swimmer.

scenes.label: wide: rivers and lakes a tiger can cross
scenes.body: That's about 5 miles of open water.

scenes.headline: Some have even been recorded hunting in water.
scenes.body: Tigers don't avoid rivers. They use them.

scenes.headline: To a tiger, a river isn't a wall. It's a road.

caption:
Tigers can swim across rivers and lakes up to 8 km wide.

No two tigers share the same stripe pattern, so researchers use stripes like fingerprints to identify wild individuals.

Source: Smithsonian's National Zoo & Conservation Biology Institute. Swimming footage: a captive tiger at Tiger Park Pattaya. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: One clean, surprising number (8 km) on moving footage, then a payoff line; the captive pool clip only illustrates swimming, never claimed as wild.
